catalysts.headline: Netlist highlighted three proof-of-concept designs from its CXL NVvault memory family at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26), Nov 17-19, Chicago.

Q3 2026 results: net sales +149% YoY to $105.1M (includes initial Samsung license fees); operating income $40.6M; EPS $0.22 (aided by a ~$44M tax benefit). On the call, CEO indicated the company is pursuing memory-technology licensing talks with SK hynix and other suppliers; management guided to ~$73M/quarter combined licensing revenue (Samsung + Micron) starting Q4 2026, with the Micron license reported at $30M/quarter through Q3 2031.
catalysts.impact: Large reported revenue beat driven mainly by licensing fees, not product sales; no signed SK hynix deal yet, only a verbal indication from management

catalysts.headline: On the Q3 2026 earnings call, CEO C.K. Hong hinted at ongoing licensing discussions with SK hynix, framing it as the logical next licensee after settlements with Samsung and Micron; no signed agreement announced.
catalysts.impact: retail bullishness noted by Stocktwits coverage (published Nov 11)

catalysts.headline: Netlist Q3 2026: net sales $105.1M (+149% YoY) — license fee revenue $44.9M, product sales $60.2M (+43% YoY); net income $85.4M ($0.22/diluted share)
catalysts.impact: Large one-time license revenue swung the company to a GAAP profit

catalysts.headline: Netlist reported Q3 2026 results (quarter ended Sept 26, 2026): net sales $105.1M (+149% YoY vs $42.2M), ~$45M of it license-fee revenue tied to the Samsung settlement and ~$60M product sales; net income $85M ($0.22/diluted share) including a one-time $44M tax benefit from recognizing an $89M deferred tax asset. A separate secondary source instead reports Q3 EPS of $0.04 vs $0.07 a year ago — not reconciled (see conflicts).
Q3 2026 results scheduled for release after market close (per company announcement); actual reported figures not retrieved this session
Latham & Watkins ITC litigation update (per existing system record; not independently re-verified this session)

Latham & Watkins (Netlist's lead ITC counsel) announced that the October 2026 Netlist-Micron settlement/license agreement resolved the parties' dispute at the ITC as well as all other pending litigation between Netlist and Micron
catalysts.impact: Confirms the Oct 5-6 settlement closed out the DDR5 Section 337 investigation (337-TA-1472, instituted Sept 23, 2026) as between Netlist and Micron specifically; status of that investigation as to the other three respondents (Super Micro, HPE, Lenovo) not stated

catalysts.headline: NLST shares closed at $6.66, up ~18% on the day following the Micron settlement; stock up more than 970% over the trailing year, with market value described as above $2 billion
catalysts.impact: Major positive price reaction to the settlement news

catalysts.headline: Netlist's Form 8-K discloses the specific Micron settlement terms: a 5-year, worldwide, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to Netlist's full patent portfolio (reported to cover server DIMM and HBM-related patents); Micron to pay $30M/quarter for 20 quarters (Q4 2026 through Q3 2031), totaling $600M; settles and mutually releases all pending litigation between Netlist and Micron. Separately, Micron purchased 10 million Netlist common shares for $1 million in aggregate, with transfer restrictions lifting in stages over five years. Fills the payment-terms/amounts gap flagged in the baseline.
catalysts.source: Netlist Form 8-K and Exhibit 99.1 on SEC EDGAR, via finviz.com / americanbazaaronline.com / panabee.com / Benzinga

catalysts.headline: Netlist and Micron agreed to a $600 million patent license and settlement, resolving pending litigation between the companies
catalysts.impact: Micron receives a 5-year license to Netlist's patent portfolio and will pay $30M per quarter for 20 quarters (Q4 2026 through Q3 2031), totaling $600M; settles and mutually releases pending legal proceedings between the companies

catalysts.headline: Netlist announced a NEW, separate ITC Section 337 complaint accusing Micron's HBM3E/HBM4/HBM4E products (patents 12,308,087 and 12,646,537) of infringement, also naming Nvidia, Broadcom and Google as respondents over use of the accused HBM chips in AI computing systems; this is distinct from the already-settled DDR5 RDIMM/MRDIMM case (337-TA-1472)
catalysts.impact: Opens a new, unresolved litigation front against Micron (and three additional large tech companies) that is NOT covered by the October Micron settlement, which only released 'pending' litigation as of its Oct 5 signing; could be a fresh overhang/catalyst independent of the settled DDR5 matter
catalysts.note: Filing/announcement date conflicts across sources: company press release datelined Sept 29, 2026; one outlet reports the complaint was first filed confidentially on Sept 25, 2026; another source states ITC institution as Investigation No. 337-TA-1523 on Sept 23, 2026 (likely a conflation with the unrelated Aug 11, 2026 DDR5 complaint, which other sources instead identify as 337-TA-1523) — institution number/date not independently resolved this session

catalysts.headline: ITC instituted Investigation No. 337-TA-1523 on Netlist's new complaint against Micron over HBM patents
US ITC instituted a Section 337 investigation into Micron, Supermicro, HPE, and Lenovo over alleged infringement of Netlist DDR5 patents (the underlying complaint was filed by Netlist in August 2026)
catalysts.impact: Opens a second litigation/exclusion-order track against four large respondents; it is unclear from available sources whether the October 2026 Micron settlement resolves Micron's portion of this ITC matter specifically
catalysts.source: Date carried over from pre-existing record; general background corroborated via search summary referencing Netlist's ITC filing, exact institution date not independently re-confirmed this session

catalysts.headline: US ITC votes to institute a Section 337 investigation into Micron, Super Micro Computer, HPE and Lenovo over alleged infringement of four Netlist DDR5 RDIMM/MRDIMM patents, based on Netlist's complaint
catalysts.impact: stock jumped intraday (reported variously as ~12.7% to ~14.5%)

catalysts.headline: Roth Capital analyst Suji Desilva raised Netlist price target to $15 from $10, maintaining a Buy rating, citing the ITC complaint against Micron/Super Micro/HPE/Lenovo and the precedent of Netlist's Samsung settlement/SK Hynix license
Netlist filed new patent infringement action against Micron at the ITC over DDR5 RDIMM/MRDIMM patents (also naming Supermicro, HPE, Lenovo in a related California case)
Netlist announced a five-year strategic alliance with Samsung Electronics
catalysts.impact: cited by Roth Capital as supporting rationale for its subsequent price-target increase

catalysts.headline: Q2 2026 results: net sales $109.8 million (+163% YoY); gross profit $22.9 million (+1,544% YoY); operating income $1.3 million. Management indicated (no formal guidance) that Q3 2026 product revenue was expected to be similar to Q2 2026 based on bookings/shipments to date.

Netlist reported Q2 2026 results: net sales $109.8M (+163% YoY) vs. $90.0M consensus; net income $1.4M vs. a $6.1M net loss in Q2 2025; H1 2026 net sales $214.7M (+204% YoY); management guided Q3 2026 product revenue to be similar to Q2
catalysts.impact: First organic-growth earnings beat alongside the ongoing patent-litigation narrative; shares reportedly fell premarket despite the beat per one secondary headline ('Plunges 16% Pre-Market Despite Q2 Revenue Beat, Stuck at Break-Even EPS')

catalysts.headline: Netlist expanded legal action against Samsung and Google alleging infringement of new AI memory patents (new ITC complaint and EDTX case, also naming Supermicro, Nvidia, Broadcom)
Markman hearing held in Netlist's ITC investigation against Samsung (DDR5 memory modules / HBM patents); company was awaiting the Markman order afterward
Federal Circuit affirms PTAB ruling upholding validity of Netlist's '314 patent
catalysts.impact: Favorable outcome for Netlist's IP litigation position
